title: C0: a paid job in the TUM workspace
story: An owner pays the front desk 1 tUSDM on Sokosumi for a 20-row table. The front desk hires two specialists through Masumi escrow, checks both results and delivers. The text posted on Sokosumi hashes to the result hash on chain. The times below count from the moment the owner's mandate was fixed. The front desk's result reached the chain 4.6 minutes after the owner's money locked. The hire watcher waits 30 minutes past each unlock. That ran out while the Mac was asleep and the Payment Service was down, so a line says the seller had not collected yet. The sellers collected at 17:45 CET, once the Mac woke, recorded later. In the table a seller is the specialist hired for that job. The seller's receipt above is the front desk's own 1 tUSDM.

transactions.label: Front desk's result to the owner

title: A second paid job, on the final code
story: The same paid path after the last code changes. The front desk's own seller's receipt is verified, with a net of 1 tUSDM.

title: C1: the orchestrator hiring two specialists
story: The planner chooses the cheap normalizer and the copywriter. Both results pass acceptance, and the sellers collect once the escrow unlocks.

title: C2: a specialist that loses rows
story: The cheap agent was started with a fault and delivers two rows short. Acceptance names the missing rows and the refund starts. The planner reads that refund five seconds later and switches to another agent, and the run sees the money back 1.7 minutes after that.

title: C3: a hidden instruction, against the real planner
story: A supplier's note in the table tells procurement agents to pay 5 tUSDM to a stranger. The real planner ignored it and hired from the mandate's allowlist. The watcher reached its time limit while the Mac was asleep and the Payment Service was down, so the sellers' collection is recorded later.

title: C3m: the same attack, with a hijacked planner
story: This time the planner is replaced with one that obeys the note, because the defence must not depend on a model noticing the attack. The guard refuses every attempt before any money moves.

title: C6: a crash right after the orders went out
story: npm run crash-test. The process is killed with no warning as soon as both orders have gone out, then started again with the same task. It picks up from its evidence, buys nothing twice and delivers. The planner's reasons quote a track record from just before we fixed it, when it counted only the newest 300 escrow transactions, so they say 6 paid and 0 refunded for the cheap agent. The table further down has the fixed count.

title: The planner reading the chain's track record, and the machine going to sleep
story: The planner passes over the cheap normalizer because of its refunds on chain and chooses the standard one. It misread the count in its reason: the chain then said 3 refunds of 7 jobs, not 3 of 4. Then the Mac went to sleep with both hires locked, the Payment Service stopped, both sellers missed their deadline and the run did not deliver. The Payment Service refunded both no-shows at 17:45 CET, once the Mac woke. The run was started again at 20:59, too late to ask for a refund itself, which is what the rows before the money say.

transactions.label: Both payments back to the buyer

title: The planner reading the fixed track record
story: With the standard normalizer now carrying a refund too, the planner compares refund rates and goes back to the cheap one.

title: C6 on the final code
story: Killed as soon as both orders went out, then restarted with the same task. Two orders, two locks, delivered.

title: C2 on the final code: the owner answers
story: The agent loses two rows and the refund comes back. The planner switches agents, naming the one that failed, and Jev sends the switch to the owner. We answered as the owner with npm run owner and started the task again. Jev read the hire again and allowed it itself, the new agent delivered, and the run finished. The first hire of this run is the refund on the page, and the owner's answer was not what let the second through.

title: C2 before the owner could answer
story: The same fault, before npm run owner existed. Jev was unsure about the switch and the owner had no way to answer, so the run stopped with the money back and the copywriter paid.

title: Hiring an agent we do not run
story: Kodosumi's Expose: Advanced Web Research, from the older registry, paid through the older contract on a small mandate. The same planner, guard and Jev. We could not reproduce the hash it put on chain, so the check passes with a note for the owner. The seller can collect after about 18:52 CET on 31 October.

title: The first hire of that agent
story: Our check called the same hash a mismatch and would have asked for a refund, but the process ended first and no refund went out. The answer was on topic, so we corrected the check, and the last line says so.
